articles.title: The Tasks for DSA After the Blue Wave
articles.author: Bread & Roses Caucus
articles.content_excerpt: On November 3rd, the American people sent a decisive message. We are sick and tired of MAGA and the Trump administration, of the cost of living crisis, of war, of corruption, of corporate greed, of billionaires dominating our political system. Alongside an overwhelming rejection of the far-right, voters also chose to send the largest number of democratic socialists in 100 years into the halls of power. Our movement elected over 100 democratic socialists with a clear message: we need a government and economy that works for working people, not the billionaires, capitalists, warmongers, and genocidaires. articles.title: Enough With the “Public Option” Already
articles.author: John Canham-Clyne
articles.content_excerpt: The difference between a vampire and a bad health care policy idea is that vampires jump out of their coffins and drink blood at sunset. Undead health care proposals emerge from think tank closets and suck the life out of useful ideas when the sun rises on a national health care debate. As public fury at exploding costs and deadly corporate claims denials boils over into historic Democratic election gains, can someone please find a wooden stake for the public option? Improved and expanded Medicare for All would give everyone full coverage at much lower cost than the combined private premiums, taxes, and out-of-pocket payments that are eating up family income today. But it violates a cardinal rule of federal politics: never do anything that causes corporations or the ultrawealthy any pain.

articles.title: The Trump Era Is Bad. But Is It Evil?
articles.author: Matt McManus
articles.content_excerpt: Leftists have an unusual relationship to the language of good and evil. On the one hand, we have a reputation for being righteous. . . . at times even self-righteous. Our publications are saturated with enough morally strident language to make a preacher blush. Even the most “scientific” of scientific socialists aren’t entirely immune, from tireless invocations of Rev Martin Luther King Jr and constant demands for justice and freedom for all to calls to end subordination and marginalization around the globe . On the other hand, leftists tend to be averse to describing structures, let alone people, as evil. Exploitative? Yes. Domineering? Of course. But evil? articles.title: In Turkey, When Does a Joke Become a Crime?
articles.author: Dora Mengüç
articles.content_excerpt: Have you ever made a joke that offended someone? Maybe they took it personally or stopped speaking to you. A joke can put strain on a relationship or leave someone feeling isolated. But what if the consequences for a joke go far beyond social fallout? What if a comedy performance lands you in a high-security prison cell? For Deniz Göktaş, this question is no longer hypothetical. Until recently, Göktaş performed for relatively small audiences, playing bars in Kadıköy, an Istanbul district known for political satire, and occasionally in university halls elsewhere in Turkey. He was part of a niche comedy scene. Things changed when he took his show to one of Istanbul’s most prominent stages and uploaded the performance to YouTube, opening it to a much wider audience. articles.title: In Finland, the Left Can Lead on Fair AI Policy
articles.author: Mike Watson
articles.content_excerpt: Finland’s next general election has been set for next April 18, hopefully bringing an end to the National Coalition Party’s current slash-and-burn coalition, in which the far-right Finns Party plays a key role. Recent polls have, however, seen the latter worryingly rise to second position, becoming the main right-wing force for the first time ever. Trailing Antti Lindtman’s Social Democrats (SDP) by 6 percentage points, the Finns Party is placing its hope in polarizing the election over immigration. But as the SDP and other left-of-center parties like the Left Alliance and the Greens seek to fend off a far-right surge, a new key battleground has emerged: artificial intelligence. articles.title: Pension Is Wall Street's Casino
articles.author: Ellen Brown/Web of Debt
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. “Most billionaires don’t park their money in making more businesses. They park their money in the stock market. That is not meaningfully investing in opportunity, it’s just investing in other billionaires.” So said Abdul El-Sayed , U.S. Senator-elect from Michigan. He said that he would rather “have an economy that makes a thousand millionaires than one billionaire,” and that money that would otherwise go into the S&P 500 should go instead to “good schools, good infrastructure, health care, child care.” It’s a laudable sentiment, but those thousand millionaires would probably still be parking their money in investments designed to make more money without producing anything.

articles.title: Remembering Dolores Huerta (1930-2026)
articles.author: DSA Religion and Socialism Working Group
articles.content_excerpt: Dolores Huerta , who died on October 28 at the age of 96, was an honorary chair of DSA from 2012-2016. But her involvement with our organization went back as far as being a speaker at a 1975 convention of one of DSA’s predecessor organizations. My wife, Dolores Delgado-Campbell, and I met her even earlier,when we were co-chairs of the United Farm Workers (UFW) lettuce boycott committee in Sacramento. We entered the fray in 1972 when the corrupt leadership of the Teamsters Union signed sweetheart contracts with grape growers, committing one of the worst examples of union betrayal in U.S. history. articles.title: Austerity Is Now the Central Conflict in Brazilian Politics
articles.author: André Singer
articles.content_excerpt: On October 4, Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, finished the first round of Brazil’s presidential election nearly two points ahead of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. Three weeks later, Lula turned the result around and won a fourth term in the October 25 runoff. In between, left-led demonstrations filled the streets of hundreds of Brazilian cities. The government also banned online betting, backed a forty-hour workweek, and raised the benefit of Bolsa Família, the cash-transfer program for poor families that Lula created in 2003. Few analysts know Lula’s political project better than André Singer. articles.author: Matt McManus
articles.content_excerpt: There is a complex debate about the extent to which socialists prioritize equality above the full flowering of each person’s individuality.
